#### Economically vital at multiple levels  
::: {.incremental}

- <h5 style="color:darkred;font-style: bold;">  Côte d’Ivoire: #1 Export  </h5>
_40% of export income, $4.95 Bi_

- <h5 style="color:darkred;font-style: bold;">  Ghana: #3 Export  </h5>
_16% of export income, $2.71 Bi_

- <h5 style="color:darkred;font-style: bold;">  Families: </h5>
_~90% of the world’s cacao is grown on small family farms._
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

<img src="images/cacao_farmer.png"  height="100%">

:::

::::




--- 

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="65%"}

<img src="images/yale360.png"  width="100%">

:::

::: {.column width="35%" .incremental}

- Cocoa cultivation is the **major driver of illegal deforestation** in Côte d’Ivoire & Ghana 

- Climate change has reduced the area suitable for Cacao farming

- **USA chocolate sales in 2025: **<h5 style="color:darkred;font-style: bold;">$28.4 bi  </h5> 
- **_per capita_ chocolate consumption in the USA:** <h5 style="color:darkred;font-style: bold;">3.7 kg/8.1 lbs</h5> 


:::
